Sports.title: Chelsea Wag shares inside snaps of trio’s controversial Madrid holiday, from private jet to loved-up pics
Sports.content:
MARC CUCURELLA’s Wag has shared pictures from a controversial Madrid holiday they took alongside his Chelsea team-mates.

The left-back and partner were joined by Enzo Fernandez and Joao Pedro along with their partners on the trip to the Spanish capital this week.





The Blues stars’ trip to Madrid comes soon after Fernandez publicly flirted with a transfer to Real Madrid.

The Argentine admitted he would like to live in the Spanish city as it reminds him of home in Buenos Aires.

As a result, now-sacked Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior suspended Fernandez for two games.

Claudia Rodríguez has now shared pictures from inside a recent trip to Spain for the Chelsea trio and their partners.

She posted on Instagram snaps that showed herself and Cucurella all loved-up.

She also included a picture of the whole group posing for the camera.

The post also gave an insight into their visit to the Madrid Open tennis tournament.

It also revealed that they travelled to the city in a private jet.



Claudia posed for a picture on the aeroplane with Valentina Cervantes and Khadije Skandar.



She captioned the post: “Madrid”

Claudia expanded on the caption with a white love heart emoji.

The Chelsea stars were also spotted at the tennis sitting in front of Los Blancos star Jude Bellingham and his brother, Borussia Dortmund ace Jobe.

The trip happened less than 24 hours after Chelsea’s FA Cup semi-final victory over Leeds United.

The players were afforded the break by interim boss Calum McFarlane.



Fernandez, 25, was the match winner at Wembley as it was his 23rd-minute header that proved to be the difference.

His agent, former Paris Saint-Germain star Javier Pastore, has since claimed there is nothing in a summer move to the Bernabeu.



The midfielder is not the only Chelsea ace tipped with an exit of Stamford Bridge this summer.

Pedro, 24, has been linked with interest from LaLiga giants Barcelona just one year after his £60million arrival.

The Brazilian is viewed as an alternative target to Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez.

The Catalan side are said to be fine with going up to £85million if it is necessary to get one of their key targets.

Sports.title: Tottenham star Guglielmo Vicario ‘reaches full transfer agreement with league champions-elect’ amid relegation battle
Sports.content:
GUGLIELMO VICARIO has taken a massive step towards leaving Tottenham this summer.

The Italian, 29, has reportedly struck a full agreement on personal terms with Serie A champions-in-waiting Inter Milan.





And the Nerazzurri are praying Spurs go down so they can nab Vicario on the cheap.

A deal would still need to be reached between the two clubs but Vicario and his agents have approved everything on the player side, according to Gazzetta dello Sport.

That means there will be no hold-ups over contract length or wages when things move forward.

Vicario is ‘ready to return’ to Serie A after three seasons and over 100 games in English football.



And Tottenham will be powerless to keep hold of him – or demand a big transfer fee – if they drop into the Championship.

Roberto De Zerbi‘s side are two points from safety with four games to play.

Inter’s fortunes could hardly be more different as they sit 10 points clear at the top of Serie A – on course to clinch their second title in three seasons.

Tottenham paid £17million to sign Vicario from Empoli in 2023 and he has two years left on his contract.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The stopper has been out of action since having hernia surgery in March, with Antonin Kinsky replacing him between the sticks.

European giants are positioning themselves to pounce on Tottenham’s top talent if they finish in the bottom three.

Barcelona have reportedly sounded out a move for Cristian Romero as a cheaper alternative to Inter’s Alessandro Bastoni.

Others could push for exits themselves due to relegation clauses automatically slashing their wages in half if they go down.

Sports.title: Watch as Cristiano Ronaldo taunts Al Ahli fans with brutal gesture during interview
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO kicked Al-Ahli fans while they were down after helping Al-Nassr beat them 2-0.

Ronaldo, 41, headed them in front from a corner in the 76th minute before Kingsley Coman sealed the result late on.





Wednesday’s crucial victory ended Al-Ahli‘s title hopes and moved Al-Nassr eight points clear at the top of the Saudi Pro League.

Al-Hilal would close the gap to five by winning their game in hand but Al-Nassr are still in a commanding position to give Ronaldo his first major trophy in Saudi football, three and a half years after he arrived.

Wounded Al-Ahli fans taunted Ronaldo after the final whistle on Wednesday by gesturing to him about their two Asian Champions League titles in a row.

They beat Kawasaki Frontale and Machida Zelvia to lift the trophy in consecutive years, while Al-Nassr have never won it.

The jibes did not bother Ronaldo, however, as he has plenty of his own silverware.

During a live TV interview, the Portuguese shouted: “Five Champions [League titles] I have.”

Ronaldo beamed as he held five fingers up to the crowd, adding: “I have five!”

One of those Champions League crowns was won at Manchester United before the veteran forward scooped up four more at Real Madrid.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He also boasts five Ballons d’Or from a glittering career that has seen him rack up a staggering 970 goals – and counting.

The absence of major Saudi silverware has been a major source of frustration for Ronaldo but that barren run will come to an end if Al-Nassr hold their nerve.

They have just four league games remaining.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid star makes dressing room feelings clear on VAR controversy
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid star makes dressing room feelings clear on VAR controversy

Arsenal’s Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid was marred by controversy with the referee pointing to the penalty spot on three occasions but one particular decision left the Gunners furious

View 2 Images Jan Oblak offered his take on the controversy against Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid star Jan Oblak claimed his side agreed with the decision to controversially chalk off Arsenal’s penalty. The Gunners thought they had won a second spot kick at the Metropolitano on Wednesday evening as Eberechi Eze was taken down by David Hancko.

‌



Referee Danny Makkelie initially gave the penalty but changed his mind after being beckoned to the VAR booth. He was shown 13 replays of the incident before deciding to cancel the spot kick.

‌



Oblak, 33, was asked for his take on the decision and claimed that the official was correct. The Slovenian stopper said: "It was an intense game from both sides. Both sides were looking for a win but I think we had a good game but at 1-1, there's a lot to decide in London next week.

‌



"There's always relief when a penalty is overturned, I hope I would have stopped it anyway. It was the referee's decision to change it and we agree with him.

"I was close to stopping the first penalty but it was just the power. He hit it with maximum power but it's in the past. We need to focus firstly on the weekend and then to London.

‌



"We will not think about the previous game where we lost 4-0 there. I believe it will be a different game and we will do everything to get a good result and get to the final.

"We don't think about lifting the trophy, first we need to work on the pitch in the second leg. Arsenal want to win the Champions League as well so we need to pass them first."

Sports.title: 'I saw Cristiano Ronaldo force manager into making radical decision - we couldn't believe it'
Sports.content:
Joleon Lescott says England players were made to pay after not knowing who Cristiano Ronaldo was during a youth match. The ex-Manchester City defender recalled that the winger forced both full-backs off in a defeat.

Before Ronaldo became a world-beating talent for the likes of Manchester United and Real Madrid, he was an 18-year-old strutting his stuff for Portugal's youth teams and Sporting CP.

In 2003, England's Under-20s faced Portugal in France and defender Lescott recounted how an unknown Ronaldo forced the manager to take off both full-backs, who had been run ragged. The star forward joined United weeks later.

You can listen to brand new episodes of In The Mixer on Spotify and Apple Podcasts!

‌



Real Madrid manager responds after Kylian Mbappe drops Jose Mourinho hint READ MORE :

Speaking on In The Mixer, brought to you by Sky Bet, Lescott said: "We played Portugal and everyone is going there and everyone knew [Ricardo] Quaresma.

"It was away. At that time. When you were sponsored, the elite players had the elite boots. You turn up there and Quaresma has got the bright orange [Nike] Vapors on.

View 3 Images Ronaldo was unknown to the Three Lions players (Image: Getty)

"Only like top players got them. You had to have a mad sponsor. But the other winger had them on. We were all thinking, 'Who is this guy?' It was him, Cristiano. We didn't know."

‌



Shaking his head in disbelief, Lescott added: "We didn't know him, but he got both full-backs subbed that game. They swapped them over and both came off!"

Nedum Onuoha, Lescott's former City team-mate, was also part of various Three Lions youth set-ups. He recalled a similar incident from a 2005 European Under-21 Championship Qualifying play-off.

"My first cycle [with the Under-21s], we had a play-off against France and it was at White Hart Lane," he said. "Walking onto the pitch before the game, not for a warm-up but to check it out, there was this weird-looking feller.

View 3 Images Onuoha played for England's youth teams (Image: In The Mixer)

‌



"Weird-looking feller walking through. Everyone's just like, 'Look at him. Who is this? Is he a player for France?' [It was] Franck Ribery. It was a two-game masterclass from Franck Ribery. Just ridiculous.

"The next time we lost in a semi-final to the Netherlands. They had Ryan Babel and loads more people like that. It's funny looking back at those times.

"I've started to realise just how many people I ended up playing with or against at that age group. I played against an Italian side with Giuseppe Rossi and some big names. I think [Giorgio] Chiellini would've been playing."

Sports.title: Mason Mount gives kids chance to live like Premier League footballers for day in first job as manager
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Mason Mount gives kids chance to live like Premier League footballers for day in first job as manager

The World Cup is be fast approaching, and this week saw England player Mason Mount make his managerial debut for a very special football match at St George's Park

View 6 Images Mason Mount and Luke Shaw give the Wishes United FC kids a pre-match pep talk

England midfielder Mason Mount was celebrating his debut as manager this week, when his team Wishes United FC slaughtered the Mascots 32-2 at St George’s Park. This was no ordinary game. The winning 11 were children with serious health conditions, who’d been treated like premier league footballers for a once-in-a-lifetime two day experience, ahead of June’s World Cup.

‌



Supported by fellow manchester-united-fc>Manchester United and England star Luke Shaw and with England star-turned Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp managing the losing side, made up of mascots from top clubs, Mason says: “I’m blown away by what we created.” One of his team’s stars, Max Shepherd, of Aylesbury, was enjoying a double celebration - as the win came on his 10th birthday. Max, who has been in remission from leukemia for two years, says: “It’s the best birthday I’ve ever had. When I grow up, I want to be a footballer. This has given me a taste of how cool it would be.”

‌



As part of the experience, the Wishes United squad stayed at the Hilton hotel. They held a press conference, like top footballers, had a team talk, were individually chauffeur driven to venues and trained with real UEFA coaches before the match - overseen by a UEFA referee.

‌



View 6 Images Max and family with Mason Mount (Image: ©Ben Walsh/Make-A-Wish UK)

At St George’s Park, in Burton Upon Trent, the Football Association’s elite national football centre - the training base for all 27 England national teams - hosts included TalkSport presenter Olivia Buzalgo and Capital radio presenter Sonny Jay. Ex lioness Lianne Sanderson and Sky Sports’ Mark McAdam were commentating.

As well as being his idea, Mason funded the event, saying: “These children have been through so much, this is a moment of joy. They threw themselves into it. There were no worries at all. For two days they didn’t have to think of anything else, just be in the moment and enjoy it.”

‌



Watched by his mum, Debbie, dad, Tony, and brother, Lewis, Mason adds: “Football has given me so much.” Of his parents, he says: “They brought me up to be a person that would always give back and help other people.”

View 6 Images Jamie Redknapp, Luke Shaw and Mason Mount watch the Wishes United FC match

Make-A-Wish grants life-changing wishes for children with critical illnesses. Jason Suckley, CEO of Make-A-Wish UK, says: “Wishes are about joy and there’s no better example of that than today.”

‌



Mason seconds that, saying: “As a child, this would have been my wish for sure. I had a dream of playing football for my country, and I’m so fortunate that it happened. These kids, through difficult and tough times, haven't had the same opportunities, so it’s amazing they’ve been able to come and see it all. That’s why we wanted to do it here as well, it’s the home of English football, you don't get much better than this.

“When I was 9,10, 11, like the kids today, I was exactly the same - so energetic, always wanting to be kicking a ball around, playing games. I’m watching now and managing Wishes United FC, thinking ‘where has the time gone?’ It's what I would have loved to be a part of at that age.”

Birthday boy Max certainly agrees, saying: “The last few years have been really tough, so it’s been nice to have a celebration today.” His mum, Laura, 37, a manager, says: “Max is football mad.”

‌



View 6 Images Finley arrives in style at Wishes FC

As for spending his birthday at St George’s Park, she adds: “It doesn’t get better. He finds it really hard to make friends, he didn’t go to school for two years, because he was going through chemo then had a bone marrow transplant. To watch him make friends here has been wonderful, so emotional. I’m so proud.”

Elsewhere, Finley Spurgeon, 9, from Poole, was having the time of his life, accompanied by his mum Anu April, 36, a civil servant, and dad Tom, 37, a business owner. Anu April, who says Finley was diagnosed with the genetic lung condition cystic fibrosis shortly after birth, was told his life expectancy was 45.

‌



Horrified to hear she might outlive her child, she adds: “Thanks to new drugs, the future looks brighter these days.” But his condition means he has to avoid situations where he could catch bacterial infections that can be life threatening - which means restricting his access to everything from school trips to jumping in puddles. Anu April says of his Wishes United experience: “He didn’t want to go to sleep on day one because then the day would be over - but then day two was even better.”

View 6 Images Robyn, 13, had such a good day and loved every second

Robyn Griffin-Briggs, 13, from Oldham, finds out tomorrow if she has the all-clear after treatment for a brain tumour. Her proud dad Simon, 36, a scaffolder, and mum Abbie, 36, a nursery practitioner, choked back emotion, after watching her Wishes United FC triumph.

‌



Simon says: “Specsavers found her brain tumour last November and she’s had surgery and proton bean treatment to remove it. It’s damaged her optic nerves, so she’s blind in her left eye and only has half the vision in her right - but she still comes to every Man U match with me.”

Abbie adds: “This wish has been amazing. I cannot thank everyone enough. Every single second we’ve been treated like royalty.” Even though his Mascots team lost, Jamie Redknapp gave a rousing appraisal of the day. He says: “It’s been an absolute pleasure to be the Mascots’ manager. It’s been a really special afternoon watching the children live out their dreams as footballers. They should be really proud of themselves."

View 6 Images Max, Mason, Luke and Olivia enjoy the very special day

‌



And Luke Shaw, who played for the senior England national team between 2019 and 2022, earning 36 caps and scoring five goals, was honoured to be part of things. He says: “The children are just so incredible - what a special day. I’m so happy I get to be a part of it. We know how much it means to them and how much they’re getting out of it. “Seeing what everyone has put into it, what Mason has put into it, I’m very proud of him.” Praising Mason’s managerial debut, he adds: “You never know where it could lead!”

Currently enjoying Man United’s success, he doesn’t know if he is going to this year’s World Cup. But, of previous England successes, he says: “Scoring for my country, that’s the pinnacle, you don’t really get higher than that. I don't know if I’ll be playing [in this year’s World Cup] or if I’ll be watching. If I’m not going, I grew up as a fan, I watched every game - so I’ll be watching, that’s not going to change. I’ll be cheering the lads on to go out there and do the best they can and try to bring it home.”

But Mason, whose career has been injury-plagued, says today belongs to Wishes United FC. Meeting the brave children had changed his outlook. He says: “It puts things like injury into perspective. I’d have them all on the squad if I was England manager. Today was really emotional. When I go to sleep tonight, I'll remember the look on the kids' faces.”

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher in passionate rant after Arsenal penalty controversy - 'It's winding me up'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher in passionate rant after Arsenal penalty controversy - 'It's winding me up'

Arsenal secured a 1-1 draw with Atletico Madrid in the first leg of their Champions League semi final and the game was marred by controversial with three penalties having been awarded

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher was left furious (Image: CBS Sports/Twitter)

Jamie Carragher has called for a Champions League rule change after being left furious by Atletico Madrid’s penalty vs Arsenal. The Spanish side were awarded a spot kick in the first half at the Metropolitano on Wednesday evening.

‌



Ben White was accused of handling the ball, with Gunners transfer target Julian Alvarez scoring from 12 yards. That came after Arsenal’s own penalty after Viktor Gyokeres scored having being taken down by David Hancko.

‌



Carragher offered his take on the home side’s spot kick and was left baffled at the award. Speaking on CBS Sports, the former Liverpool defender said: “What’s he supposed to do? He has fallen down trying to block a shot. It’s winding me up! The thought of a Champions League final being decided on that…

‌



“I’m not having it. It’s not right, it’s not fair. I just think it’s gone far too far. Don’t get me wrong, as soon as I saw the incident, I knew it was going to be a penalty. This is the Champions League way of doing it.

Diego Simeone speaks out on Arsenal controversy after angry tunnel bust-up READ MORE :

Diego Simeone confronts Ben White in furious tunnel bust-up after Arsenal match READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“But honestly, if we go to Budapest and someone wins the Champions League on one of these ridiculous handballs, it’s a stain on the Champions League. The Champions League is the best competition in the world by a mile. The World Cup can’t come close, no domestic division can come close. The only thing letting it down is this.

‌



”You’re just thinking this is ridiculous. You’ve got the best players in the world competing for the biggest trophy they can win in club football. And something like that is going to decide a game at this level. It’s not right. It’s not fair on the players. Nobody likes it.”

Asked by punditry colleague Thierry Henry what Carragher wanted to see in the competition going forwards, he replied: “It’s just a bit of common sense.

“The first thing that would stop the two penalties we saw the last two nights, if something hits another part of your body and then hits your arm, it’s not a penalty!”

‌



View 2 Images Atletico Madrid were awaded a penalty after Ben White's handball (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was unsurprisingly one of those left furious at the final whistle in Madrid. But instead, he hit out at the decision to chalk off Arsenal’s late spot kick.

Eberechi Eze was taken down but the referee overturned his decision following a VAR review. Arteta said: "Well after going into the dressing room and speaking to the boys and understanding and watching the penalty incident for the second one, getting it overturned, extremely disappointed and annoyed because it was against the rules and I don't understand it. It changes the course of the tie, so very, very upset."

Sports.title: Declan Rice lets rip after Arsenal VAR controversy and shares why referee changed his mind
Sports.content:
Declan Rice lets rip after Arsenal VAR controversy and shares why referee changed his mind

Arsenal were on what they perceived to be the wrong end of two VAR decisions in their Champions League semi-final first leg against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday night

View 2 Images Declan Rice spoke about the controversial incidents in Arsenal's Champions League semi-final against Atletico Madrid

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has hit out after the Gunners controversially had a late penalty overturned during their Champions League semi-final showdown with Atletico Madrid. The England star accused referee Danny Makkelie of being swayed by the home crowd after Eberechi Eze was brought down by David Hancko's outstretched right leg.

‌



With just ten minutes remaining on the clock, Makkelie pointed to the spot, before VAR stepped in and the referee sensationally reversed his original decision. Speaking after the final whistle, Rice took aim at UEFA officials for handling matches to a different standard compared to the Premier League, saying: "UEFA (Champions League) is totally different, I think. In both boxes you have to be so careful because they give absolutely everything.

‌



"The second one, Ebs' one, it's a clear penalty. I don't know how that's not been given. I think the fans provoked the decision and changed the ref's mind. But it doesn't matter, we move on to next week and we want to beat them at home."

‌



It was the second VAR intervention of the evening to go against the visitors, following Ben White being judged to have handled Marcos Llorente's volley, which Julian Alvarez coolly converted from the spot. "I've not seen it back yet," Rice told Stan Sport straight after the final whistle. "At first glance I thought that maybe if it's in the Premier League it doesn't get given because it's so low to the ground.

Diego Simeone speaks out on Arsenal controversy after angry tunnel bust-up READ MORE :

Diego Simeone behaviour branded ‘awful’ as pundits all agree on Arsenal penalty controversy READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"The ball's not going on target. But then UEFA (matches) are totally different rules...hands away from the body. I think with UEFA they give it but Premier League, I'm not so sure."

‌



When pushed on why he believed the rules differed, Rice said: "It's just the way it's operated, I think. I feel like they penalise you more in European competitions.

"I've felt that since I played in the Champions League three years ago. Referees are really quick to make decisions, to blow their whistle. You can't do much about it. You've just got to watch out and be careful."

View 2 Images Ebere Eze thought he won Arsenal a penalty but the decision was overturned (Image: AP)

‌



Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was equally incensed by the incidents. He said: "In the manner that we conceded the penalty, we were disappointed. In the Premier League, it's not a penalty, but here I have to accept that this is handball.

"But what I'm incredibly fuming with is how the hell the penalty on Eze gets overturned in the manner that it happened when there is no clear and obvious error? And this changes the course of the game. And at this level, I'm sorry but this cannot happen.

"When a referee has to watch it 13 times, what is clear about that? It's impossible and we are all fuming about it. We need to apply the rules.

Article continues below

"When you have fought so hard for nine months to be in this position, that goal could have completely changed the course of the tie. And it cannot happen. I'm sorry. We put so much on it. So, so, so much on it. This cannot happen."

When pressed on whether he would raise the matter with UEFA, Arteta responded: "I think that it's up to the club to decide the best thing to do. Now they're not going to give us a penalty. That's gone. And that's it. That's over."

Sports.title: Diego Simeone speaks out on Arsenal controversy after angry tunnel bust-up
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone speaks out on Arsenal controversy after angry tunnel bust-up

Arsenal’s first-leg of their Champions League semi final clash with Atletico Madrid was plagued by controversial penalty decisions, with both managers left unhappy at the final whistle

View 2 Images Diego Simeone has offered his take on the controversial penalty decisions in Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone had his own complaints about the penalty controversy that blighted the Spanish side’s Champions League clash with Arsenal. Three spot kicks were awarded at the Metropolitano on Wednesday evening.

‌



The first saw the Premier League side awarded a penalty after Viktor Gyokeres was taken down - the Swedish striker scoring. Atleti were then given their own as Julian Alvarez netted from 12 yards following an apparent handball from Ben White.

‌



Arsenal thought they had been given their second penalty of the game as David Hancko stood on Eberechi Eze’s foot. But referee Danny Makkelie changed his mind after watching multiple replays at the VAR booth.

‌



That was a decision that left Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta incensed. Speaking after the game, the Spaniard said: "Well after going into the dressing room and speaking to the boys and understanding and watching the penalty incident for the second one, getting it overturned, extremely disappointed and annoyed because it was against the rules and I don't understand it. It changes the course of the tie, so very, very upset."

Diego Simeone behaviour branded ‘awful’ as pundits all agree on Arsenal penalty controversy READ MORE :

Steven Gerrard clashes with Martin Keown over Mikel Arteta behaviour after Arsenal draw READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Atleti head coach Simeone has now given his take on the decisions. He said: “In my opinion, the first penalty involved contact from behind, the player anticipated the contact and went down. In Champions League semi-finals, you need a penalty that is truly a penalty.

‌



“The referee understood that it was. On the other occasion, thanks to VAR, he understood that it was a penalty because initially it wasn’t a handball, and then, in the second instance, also thanks to VAR, it wasn’t a penalty.

“VAR sometimes gives you the benefit of the doubt and sometimes it takes it away.”

Arsenal and Atletico Madrid will renew their rivalry next week for the second leg at the Emirates Stadium. And Simeone has sent his side a rousing message ahead of that game.

‌



View 2 Images Diego Simeone has given his verdict on Atletico Madrid's clash with Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

He added: “I rarely remember this atmosphere at the start of the match. Tremendous, wonderful, a gift to the team. The first half was calmer, with one chance for Julián and one for them.

“In the second half we adjusted more, you could see their fatigue from so many games that they’ve played, that they have to win the Premier League, the Champions League.

‌



“In the second half we could have taken the lead, but their goalkeeper had good saves, a defender saved one from Griezmann. We have an extraordinary challenge ahead of us: London, Arsenal’s ground. We will go and play with everything.”

Simeone was involved in an incident after the game as he appeared to clash with Arsenal defender White.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo involved in huge bust-up as Al-Nassr match ends in complete chaos
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo involved in huge bust-up as Al-Nassr match ends in complete chaos

Al-Nassr edged closer to the Saudi Pro League title on Wednesday evening thanks to a 2-0 win over Al-Ahli, with chaos ensuing in the aftermath as tensions boiled over

View 2 Images Things turned ugly in the aftermath of Al-Nassr's win over Al-Ahli (Image: X)

Cristiano Ronaldo was part of the chaos unfolding in the aftermath of Al-Nassr's 2-0 win over Al-Ahli. The two teams met in the Saudi Pro League on Wednesday evening at the Alawwal Park.

‌



Al-Nassr ultimately secured victory thanks to goals from Ronaldo and Kingsley Coman, extending their lead over Al-Hilal at the top of the league standings to eight points as they surge into their final four with momentum. It also came as the club's 16th win in the league in a row and their 20th consecutive across all competitions.

‌



But while there should have been jubilation in front of a jam-packed home crowd after their win over Al-Ahli, the mood quickly turned sour. Merih Demiral was spotted arguing with Ronaldo immediately after the full-time whistle, as he was held back by players and staff.

‌



He then quickly made a bee-line for Coman, as the Frenchman was spotted gesturing at him before skipping away. Nawaf Boushal was also spotted gesturing furiously and exchanging words with Ivan Toney, before the Englishman retreated away from the fracas.

Demiral was then spotted picking up one of his two Asian Champions League medals, before putting it round his neck and showing it off to Al-Nassr fans, biting it while furious first-pumping in further antagonization.

Cristiano Ronaldo on collision course with Lionel Messi after major announcement READ MORE :

Mohamed Simakan, meanwhile, ran a victory lap of the stadium with a large Al-Nassr flag in hand, distancing himself from the skirmish after waving it in front of Demiral. He later handed the flag to Ronaldo, who was spotted laughing and joking with his team-mate before attempting to plant it in the turf.

‌



After tensions had cooled and Al-Ahli players and staff had left the pitch, Al-Nassr players enjoyed a celebration with fans. Ronaldo was also spotted taking a jab at Demiral in his post-match interview, laughing as he said: "Five Champions, I have. I have five, five."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

When asked about the wealth of "stress" in the game and aftermath, he also explained that he plans on speaking with league officials this summer, appalled by consistent "bad things" and complaints. He added: "I think this is not good for the league.

‌



"Everyone complains, everyone does it more than they should do. This is football, this is not a war.

"We know we have to fight, everyone wants to win, but it's not allowed, everything. It's not allowed, everything.

"I'm going to have time to speak at the end of the season because I see many, many, many bad things. Many players complain, doing posts on Instagram and Facebook.

‌



"Speak about the referees, speak about the league, speak about the project. I think this is not good. This is not the goal of the league.

"We should give examples, not only here, but also for Europe. We want to compete with them to be one of the best leagues in the world. But like that, I think we should analyse. Stop that, speak with the SPL because, for me, this is not football."

However, the beef didn't finish on the pitch, as Demiral was spotted leaving telling the media that he felt cheated as his team left the stadium. He said: "All the referees, wallahi, crazy, my friends.

"The reputation of the league, how are you supposed to...check here [pointing towards his leg following a tackle during the match]. Check my foot, he broke, almost, my foot, huh?

Sports.title: Tottenham's ideal 2026/27 squad - Rashford chance and £21m man joins De Zerbi rebuild
Sports.content:
Tottenham's ideal 2026/27 squad - Rashford chance and £21m man joins De Zerbi rebuild

Tottenham Hotspur's squad could be hugely different next season if the club avoid Premier League relegation

View 4 Images Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi faces a pivotal summer transfer window (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside, Offside via Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur face a string of major decisions in the summer transfer window, provided the club manage to secure Premier League survival. New boss Roberto De Zerbi may look to shake up his squad significantly to ensure Spurs don't find themselves embroiled in another relegation battle.

‌



It has been a thoroughly miserable season for Tottenham, who claimed their first league victory since December only last weekend. The side sit two points from safety with four matches remaining to preserve their top-flight status.

‌



Should Spurs accomplish their goal, De Zerbi will be eager to reshape his options. Here, Mirror Football takes a look at how a dream Spurs squad could line up for the 2026/27 Premier League campaign.

‌



Goalkeepers

Guglielmo Vicario has been first choice since his arrival in 2023, but Spurs could be poised to ring the changes in goal. The 29-year-old is reportedly on Inter Milan's radar and De Zerbi may put his trust in another pair of hands.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Antonin Kinsky has looked composed in his recent outings, recovering well from his major setback against Atletico Madrid earlier this term. The 23-year-old would be handed the opportunity to step up as number one should Vicario choose to depart.

‌



Tottenham face uphill relegation battle after injury crisis reaches worrying new low READ MORE :

The Daily Mail has linked Spurs with an interest in Freiburg and Germany U21 international Noah Atubolu, who could offer genuine competition for Kinsky. Meanwhile, Brandon Austin holds on to his place as third-choice goalkeeper.

Defenders

Securing Premier League survival would enable Spurs to retain key defensive figures such as Cristian Romero, Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie. However, the club could look to cash in on Micky van de Ven, linked with both Liverpool and Manchester United, having fallen short of their seasonal targets and missed out on European football.

Offloading Van de Ven would create a gap in De Zerbi's team for Bournemouth defender Marcos Senesi, who is expected to become a free agent. The 28-year-old has emerged as a top target and securing top-flight status would be crucial in getting that deal over the line. Similarly, Andy Robertson could link up with De Zerbi's squad following his departure from Liverpool.

‌



View 4 Images Bournemouth's Marcos Senesi could join as a free agent (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

Young loanee Luka Vuskovic will return from Hamburg to provide defensive cover alongside Kevin Danso, while Radu Dragusin finds a move elsewhere. At full-back, Djed Spence offers an alternative option to Porro, while promising young left-back Souza will head out on loan following Robertson's arrival. Spurs maintaining their Premier League status would also see Ben Davies depart at the end of his contract this summer.

Midfielders

Avoiding relegation would pave the way for Joao Palhinha's loan move from Bayern Munich to be made permanent for around £21.7million. De Zerbi is already well-equipped in the middle of the park but is unlikely to sanction moves for the likes of Archie Gray and Lucas Bergvall as part of his rebuilding project.

‌



Pape Matar Sarr is reported to be in discussions over a switch to Fenerbahce and would be permitted to depart, while Yves Bissouma is approaching the final months of his contract. The Spurs manager will ideally be strengthened by the return of duo James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski following lengthy spells on the sidelines.

View 4 Images Joao Palhinha has impressed during his loan spell (Image: Andrew Kearns - CameraSport via Getty Images)

The pair will offer competition for Xavi Simons, who sustained his own injury setback at the weekend. Meanwhile, Rodrigo Bentancur and Conor Gallagher provide further options in the centre of the park.

‌



Forwards

Spurs could be poised to make multiple alterations in attack following a frustrating season. Randal Kolo Muani is unlikely to stay beyond his loan spell while Richarlison and Mathys Tel have struggled to propel Spurs towards safety.

The club have been linked with a surprise swoop for Marcus Rashford should he be unable to secure a permanent transfer to Barcelona. The England international would establish himself on the left wing, with Wilson Odobert offering another alternative.

View 4 Images Spurs have been linked with Marcus Rashford (Image: Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



Spurs could retain their Premier League status at West Ham's expense, which would create an opportunity for De Zerbi to capture Hammers captain Jarrod Bowen in another statement signing. A fully fit Mohammad Kudus would have competition on the right wing.

Dominic Solanke would remain as the focal point in attack. However, Al-Hilal striker Marcos Leonardo may emerge as a fresh backup option after being linked with a switch to Spurs. The 22-year-old Brazilian previously played for Santos and Benfica before joining the Saudi Pro League side.

Spurs' 25-man squad: Kinsky, Atubolu, Austin; Porro, Spence, Romero, Sensei, Vuskovic, Danso, Robertson, Udogie; Palhinha, Bergvall, Gray, Gallagher, Bentancur, Simons, Maddison, Kulusevski; Bowen, Kudus, Rashford, Odobert; Leonardo, Solanke.

Sports.title: Williamson signs new Arsenal contract
Sports.content:
Leah Williamson has signed a new contract with Arsenal Women.

The 29-year-old's season has been hampered by injury, missing the first half of the campaign with a knee problem sustained during Euro 2025 and making just 10 appearances so far in all competitions.

The defender played her first 90 minutes in the Women's Super League in January and started in Arsenal's 2-1 win over Lyon in the first leg of their Champions League semi-final on Sunday before scoring after coming off the bench in the 7-0 thrashing of Leicester on Tuesday.

Williamson has played 282 times for Arsenal and scored 17 goals since joining two decades ago and has gone on to become vice-captain.

The centre-back lifted the Champions League trophy with captain Kim Little last season and has one Women's Super League title, four League Cups, two FA Cups and one FIFA Women's Champions Cup to her name during her 12 years in the Arsenal first team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's Super League match between Arsenal and Leicester

For the Lionesses, Williamson led the team to back-to-back European Championship titles in 2022 and 2025 and has won 67 caps, scoring five times.

On Tuesday, Arsenal extended the contract of defender Steph Catley, while striker Stina Blackstenius renewed her deal last week and Little has signed for an additional year.

More to follow.

Sports.title: UEFA releases statement on Arsenal penalty decision as Dermot delivers verdict
Sports.content:
UEFA has released a statement to explain why Arsenal had a late penalty overturned in their Champions League semi-final first leg at Atletico Madrid.

Substitute Eberechi Eze initially earned a spot-kick after going down under a challenge from Atletico defender David Hancko after 78 minutes.

Despite contact being made with Eze's foot, the VAR intervened to recommend referee Danny Makkelie review the incident at his on-screen monitor.

After watching multiple replays, Makkelie decided to rule out the penalty-kick, a decision Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta slammed as "completely unacceptable", and the game finished 1-1 ahead of the second leg next Tuesday.

Image: David Hancko challenges Eberechi Eze - but the initial penalty call was overturned

In a brief statement, UEFA explained the decision: "Atleti player, No 17, did not commit a foul on the opponent."

European football's governing body declined to provide any further clarification about the decision-making process for the penalty overturn when approached by Sky Sports News.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Athletic's David Ornstein was puzzled as to why Arsenal controversially had a second penalty overturned by VAR in their Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid

UEFA said upon introduction of the technology that "the VAR team will check all match-changing situations but only intervene for clear and obvious mistakes".

Dermot: Not enough to overturn penalty

Former Premier League official Dermot Gallagher on Sky Sports News:

"If you look at one of the angles, it looks like Eze is clearly fouled; another angle is inconclusive. Rather than look at inconclusive angles, look at conclusive ones. The referee thinks it is a penalty on the field. The VAR, I think, looks at it too much.

"People asked me if it is enough to give a penalty. Once the referee gives the penalty, the question has to be 'is it enough to turn over?'.

"One angle it looks like he catches him on the top of the foot. The defender definitely doesn't get the ball. That is all in Eze's favour.

"Is it enough to turn over? I think not. I don't think it is the most obvious penalty in the world, but once it is given, it is given.

"Once it is given, it has to be clear and obvious. There is not enough to overturn it."

Arteta fumes over penalty decision

Warren explained: "It wouldn't surprise me. Tyson wants to keep busy. Tyson has to have focus in his life as far as boxing is concerned. It's having a date. And at this moment there is no date [for the Joshua fight] because obviously AJ's fighting in July."

Joshua losing to Kristian Prenga, the little known Albanian he will fight in the summer, could be a problem for the Fury fight going ahead.

Warren concluded: "Hopefully there's going to be no hiccups and we'll get it.

Sports.title: Real Madrid president Perez keen on Mourinho reunion but no approach made
Sports.content:
Club president Florentino Perez is thought to be keen on Jose Mourinho returning to Real Madrid but Sky Sports News understands no approach has been made for the Portuguese manager.

Perez is heading the search for a new boss at the Bernabeu, with Alvaro Arbeloa, who took over from Xabi Alonso in January, expected to be replaced at the end of the season.

Perez remains close to Mourinho and is thought to be keen on a reunion with the 63-year-old, who won the LaLiga title at Real Madrid with a record 100 points 14 years ago.

However, there has been no official contact so far with the Benfica boss, who is in no immediate hurry to decide his future.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol discusses the possibility of Jose Mourinho returning to Real Madrid

Benfica, who are seven points behind league leaders Porto, are three games away from becoming the only team in Europe to achieve an invincible league season. Three wins would also secure a second-place finish in the Portuguese Primeira Liga ahead of local rivals Sporting, and the prospect of Champions League football next season.

Mourinho is aware of all the speculation surrounding his future, including suggestions that he's top of Real Madrid's wanted list, but is understood to want to concentrate on those two big targets with Benfica.

Mourinho has also been linked with several other top clubs and the Portugal national team job. Portugal will co-host the World Cup in 2030.
